transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm explaining this the right way, but... I guess what brought me in is I just don't feel like myself anymore. 

It's probably nothing major, I don't want to make a big fuss out of it, but I've noticed I barely talk to people lately. I just sort of... go flat and quiet. And at work—I clean buildings—even just getting started on my cleaning route, it feels like pushing a loaded cart uphill. I just can't seem to get moving like I used to. 

Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm giving you the kind of information you need.
Have you noticed that you don't enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you've lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Well... yeah, I think you hit the nail on the head there, doctor. I hope it's alright to admit this, I really don't want to sound lazy or anything. But... I used to really look forward to my routines, you know? Going fishing on Saturdays, or just sitting down with my coffee to do the crossword. Even at work, I used to get a kick out of showing the younger guys some tricks for stripping a floor properly. 

But lately... I don't know. I guess I mostly just let those things sit. It's not that I'm trying to be difficult or slack off, it's just... doing them doesn't really give me anything back anymore, if that makes sense? 

I hope I'm answering your question right. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. I hope I don't sound like I'm complaining, because I know people have it a lot worse, but... the feeling down part, it's been hanging around for about a year and two months. 

It started up not too long after I moved. I thought maybe I was just taking a bit to settle in, you know? I didn't want to make a fuss about it at first. But it just sort of stuck around. Is that... is that a normal amount of time for something like this to last? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture.
Have you noticed that your movements or thoughts have become slower, or that even small tasks leave you feeling very tired?

Well, um... I guess so, yes. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses for not working hard enough. I really try to push through it. But, um... yeah, even if I sleep straight through the night, by the time I get to the building to start my shift, my arms and legs just feel so heavy. 

And then... well, even small jobs, like hauling the trash bags out to the dumpster, they just wear me out a lot more than they should. I feel bad even bringing it up, because I know it's my job and I should just be able to do it, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just getting lazy in my old age. Does that make sense, though? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you found yourself feeling like a failure or blaming yourself for things more than usual?

Well... I guess I have been a little hard on myself lately. I really hope I don't sound like I'm just throwing a pity party or anything. I know I should just count my blessings. 

But, um... yeah, I do catch myself thinking that I've let people down. Especially since I lost my old place. I just keep feeling like I should have been able to keep things together better, you know? And lately, it just sort of spirals. Like... if the church pantry is running low on supplies, or if one of the other guys misses a spot in a hallway at work... my mind just immediately goes to how it's somehow my fault. 

I know it probably sounds silly when I say it out loud. I'm really trying not to think that way, I promise. Is it... is it normal to get stuck on thoughts like that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Well, um... I suppose my eating habits might have changed a little bit. I really don't want to sound ungrateful, because I know how lucky I am to be able to buy groceries at all. But... well, to be completely honest, most days lately, food just sort of... tastes like cardboard to me. 

So I guess I have been skipping meals here and there, or maybe just having a few crackers when I finish my cleaning shift. And... yeah, my work pants have been hanging a bit looser than they used to. I just pull my belt a notch tighter, so it's really not a huge problem or anything! I'm still getting by just fine. But, um, is it normal for your appetite to just disappear like that? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.
Have you ever felt so down or hopeless that you've thought about hurting yourself or ending your life?

Well, um... I really don't want to alarm you or anything. I know it's a heavy question, and I'm really trying my best to stay positive, I promise I am. 

But, um... well, to be perfectly honest... I don't have some big plan or anything like that. I wouldn't do that. But... a lot of mornings lately, I just wake up and catch myself thinking that maybe it would just be easier if I hadn't woken up at all. 

I feel terrible even admitting that, because I know I shouldn't think that way. It actually scares me a bit, which is why I'm trying to be honest with you about it now. I hope it's okay that I shared that... I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right pieces so you can help me. Is it... is it common for people to feel that way when things get hard?
